self_correction.what_I_got_wrong_twice: I twice concluded the transfer had stalled by polling the blob file size with Get-ChildItem. On Windows the reported length of a file being actively written lags, so a growing download can appear frozen. I killed a download at what turned out to be 2157 MB of 2610 MB on that false reading.
self_correction.correct_method: wait on process exit, or inspect the .incomplete blob length via a fresh handle; do not infer liveness from a cached directory listing
self_correction.why_it_is_recorded: the same mistake would corrupt any future judgement about acquisition feasibility, and constraint 10 requires the actual technical cause

compute_environment_measured.assessment: compute is adequate for a frozen 650M forward at window 1000, batch 1. Nothing about the GPU blocked this step.

acquisition_observations.observed_pattern: the transfer runs for several hundred MB to about 2.1 GB, the connection drops, and the retry begins a NEW .incomplete blob from zero instead of resuming the existing one. Progress is therefore not cumulative across attempts.
acquisition_observations.diagnosis: sustained large-object throughput through the local proxy is unreliable, and the client restarts rather than range-resumes. This is an acquisition-infrastructure failure. It is not connectivity, not credentials, not licence, not disk space and not GPU capacity.
